def-qftx-nonabelian-gauge-data:
## Definition

Assume the axiom of countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, second-countable smooth manifold without boundary. A **non-Abelian gauge datum on $M$** consists of the following specified objects.

First choose a finite-dimensional real Lie group $G$ that is compact in its manifold topology (every open cover has a finite subcover) and noncommutative (there are $g,h\in G$ with $gh\ne hg$). The actual group $G$, including its global form, is part of the datum. Its Lie algebra is $\mathfrak g=\operatorname{Lie}(G)=T_eG$ with the bracket transported from left-invariant smooth vector fields.

Choose a smooth right principal $G$-bundle $\pi:P\to M$: the projection and right action are smooth, the action is free and transitive on each fibre, and there are local trivializations $\pi^{-1}(U)\cong U\times G$ that are equivariant diffeomorphisms over each open $U\subseteq M$.

Choose a specified set $I$ of representation labels and, for each $a\in I$, a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V_a$, a positive-definite Hermitian form $h_a$, and a smooth group homomorphism $\rho_a:G\to U(V_a,h_a)$. Here $U(V_a,h_a)$ is the group of complex-linear isometries of $h_a$, and a representation is the corresponding finite-dimensional group action. Its associated vector bundle is the quotient $E_a=P\times_{\rho_a}V_a$ with relation $[pg,v]=[p,\rho_a(g)v]$.

Two smooth right principal $G$-bundles over $M$ are isomorphic over $M$ when a smooth diffeomorphism between their total spaces covers $\operatorname{id}_M$ and commutes with the right $G$-actions. A **bundle sector** is one equivalence class under this relation. The datum specifies a set $\Sigma$ of admitted bundle sectors and requires $[P]\in\Sigma$; a model may take $\Sigma=\{[P]\}$. The Lie algebra alone does not replace the chosen group or sector. This definition does not choose a connection, an action functional, or a quantum theory.
def-qftx-principal-connection-form:
## Definition

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, and let $\pi:P\to M$ be a smooth right principal $G$-bundle for a finite-dimensional real Lie group $G$, with $\mathfrak g=\operatorname{Lie}(G)=T_eG$. A supplied principal connection is a smooth, right-invariant complement $TP=VP\oplus H$, where $VP=\ker d\pi$; write $v:TP\to VP$ for the projection along $H$, and let $K_H(X,Y)=-v([hX,hY])$ be its vertical-valued curvature. For $Z\in\mathfrak g$ and $p\in P$, define the fundamental vertical vector $Z_P(p)=\left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_{t=0}p\exp_G(tZ)$. The orbit differential $\zeta_p: \mathfrak g\to V_pP$, $Z\mapsto Z_P(p)$, is a linear isomorphism, as proved below. Define the **principal connection 1-form** by

$$\omega_p(X):=\zeta_p^{-1}(v_pX),\qquad X\in T_pP.$$

Then $\omega$ is a smooth $\mathfrak g$-valued 1-form satisfying $\omega(Z_P)=Z$, $\ker\omega=H$, and $R_g^*\omega=\operatorname{Ad}_{g^{-1}}\omega$ for every fixed $g\in G$. Conversely, a smooth $\mathfrak g$-valued 1-form with the reproduction and equivariance properties determines the principal connection $H=\ker\omega$. The converted vertical curvature $\kappa_H:=\omega\circ K_H$ is a $\mathfrak g$-valued alternating 2-form; its equality with the Cartan curvature is established in the curvature lemma.
def-qftx-lie-algebra-valued-form-bracket:
## Definition

Let $M$ be a smooth manifold and $\mathfrak g$ a finite-dimensional real Lie algebra. For homogeneous $\alpha\in\Omega^p(M,\mathfrak g)$ and $\beta\in\Omega^q(M,\mathfrak g)$, define their **graded bracket** by

$$[\alpha\wedge\beta](X_1,\ldots,X_{p+q}) := \frac{1}{p!q!}\sum_{\sigma\in S_{p+q}}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)[\alpha(X_{\sigma(1)},\ldots,X_{\sigma(p)}),\beta(X_{\sigma(p+1)},\ldots,X_{\sigma(p+q)})].$$

Here $\Omega^p(M,\mathfrak g)$ is the space of smooth alternating $p$-linear forms with values in $\mathfrak g$, the inner bracket is the Lie-algebra bracket, and the sum is over all permutations. This is a smooth $\mathfrak g$-valued $(p+q)$-form. It obeys graded skew-symmetry $[\alpha\wedge\beta]=-(-1)^{pq}[\beta\wedge\alpha]$, graded Jacobi

$$\left[\alpha\wedge\left[\beta\wedge\gamma\right]\right]=\left[\left[\alpha\wedge\beta\right]\wedge\gamma\right]+(-1)^{pq}\left[\beta\wedge\left[\alpha\wedge\gamma\right]\right],$$

and the exterior-derivative rule

$$d[\alpha\wedge\beta]=[d\alpha\wedge\beta]+(-1)^p[\alpha\wedge d\beta].$$

In particular, for $\mathfrak g$-valued 1-forms $A,B$, $[A\wedge B](X,Y)=[A(X),B(Y)]-[A(Y),B(X)]$, so $\tfrac12[A\wedge A](X,Y)=[A(X),A(Y)]$. This fixes the normalization used by the Cartan curvature formula.
lem-qftx-principal-curvature-cartan-bian:
## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, and let $\pi:P\to M$ be a smooth right principal $G$-bundle with a principal connection form $\omega$ associated to $H$, using $Z_P(p)=\left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_0p\exp_G(tZ)$ for the right action. For Lie-algebra-valued forms use the graded bracket defined by alternating shuffle and the Lie bracket; in degree one, $[A\wedge B](X,Y)=[A(X),B(Y)]-[A(Y),B(X)]$. Define

$$\Omega_\omega:=d\omega+\frac12[\omega\wedge\omega],\qquad D_\omega\eta:=d\eta+[\omega\wedge\eta].$$

Then $\Omega_\omega$ is horizontal and $\operatorname{Ad}$-equivariant, and $\Omega_\omega=\omega\circ K_H$ for the imported vertical-valued curvature $K_H(X,Y)=-v([hX,hY])$. For any trivializing cover with smooth sections $s_i:U_i\to P$, set $A_i=s_i^*\omega$ and $F_i=s_i^*\Omega_\omega$. On an overlap, let $g_{ij}:U_i\cap U_j\to G$ be the smooth map determined by $s_j=s_i g_{ij}$, and write $\theta_L(g_{ij})=g_{ij}^*\theta_L$ for the left Maurer–Cartan form. Then

$$A_j=\operatorname{Ad}_{g_{ij}^{-1}}A_i+\theta_L(g_{ij}),\qquad F_i=dA_i+\frac12[A_i\wedge A_i],\qquad F_j=\operatorname{Ad}_{g_{ij}^{-1}}F_i,\qquad D_{A_i}F_i=0,$$

where $D_{A_i}\eta:=d\eta+[A_i\wedge\eta]$. The transition equations concern changes of local sections; they do not identify an arbitrary map $M\to G$ with a global automorphism of a nontrivial bundle.
def-qftx-associated-covariant-derivative:
## Definition

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional smooth manifold, $G$ a finite-dimensional real Lie group, $\pi:P\to M$ a smooth right principal $G$-bundle, and $\omega$ the principal connection 1-form of a supplied horizontal distribution. Fix a finite-dimensional complex representation $\rho:G\to\operatorname{GL}_{\mathbb C}(V)$ that is smooth, and let $E=P\times_\rho V$ be its associated vector bundle with relation $[pg,v]=[p,\rho(g)v]$. Define $\rho_*:=d\rho_e:\mathfrak g\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, where the differential is taken after viewing $\rho$ as a smooth matrix-valued map. For any open cover with smooth local sections $s_i:U_i\to P$, write $A_i=s_i^*\omega$. A smooth section $\sigma$ of $E$ has unique local components $\psi_i:U_i\to V$ given by $\sigma(x)=[s_i(x),\psi_i(x)]$. Define the **associated covariant derivative** $\nabla^\omega\sigma$ by its local components

$$
(\nabla^\omega\sigma)_i=d\psi_i+\rho_*(A_i)\psi_i,
$$

where $(\rho_*(A_i)\psi_i)(X)=\rho_*(A_i(X))\psi_i$ for $X\in TU_i$. These expressions patch to a smooth $E$-valued 1-form on $M$, independently of the chosen local sections, and satisfy $\nabla^\omega(f\sigma)=df\otimes\sigma+f\nabla^\omega\sigma$ for every smooth scalar function $f$ on $M$.
